title: Coordinate Geometry
notes: Distance formula comes straight from Pythagoras Theorem applied to the coordinate plane.
Distance of a point from the origin is a special case of the distance formula with the second point as (0,0).

Collinearity check: three points are collinear if the distance between the outer two equals the sum of distances of the middle point to each (i.e. AB+BC=AC), OR if the area of the triangle they form is zero.

To identify quadrilateral type from 4 points: compute all 4 sides and both diagonals using distance formula, then compare (all sides equal + diagonals equal = square; all sides equal + diagonals unequal = rhombus; opposite sides equal + diagonals equal = rectangle; etc).
Section formula gives the point dividing a segment in a given ratio internally -- derived using AA similarity of triangles (links back to Chapter 6).
Midpoint formula is just the section formula with ratio 1:1.
For 'point dividing a line in ratio k:1' problems, or 'find the ratio' problems, set up the section formula and solve for the unknown ratio or coordinate.

formulas.name: Distance Formula
formulas.use: Distance between any two points P(x1,y1), Q(x2,y2).

formulas.name: Section Formula (internal division)
formulas.use: Point dividing segment AB in ratio m1:m2 from A.

formulas.name: Midpoint Formula
formulas.use: Special case of section formula with ratio 1:1.

examples.question: Find the distance between P(4,6) and Q(6,8).
A relay tower P divides segment AB (A at origin, B(36,15)) so that distance from B is twice distance from A -- ratio 1:2. Find P.
examples.solution: Using section formula with m1:m2=1:2: x=(1x36+2x0)/3=12, y=(1x15+2x0)/3=5. So P=(12,5).
